full_judgment: 2. The plaintiffs' case in short, is that the suit jotes originally belonged to Baidyaram Sarker and Raj Mohan Sarker in equal share. Raj Mohan died leaving behind son Raj Kanta, putrabati daughter Joshoda and wife Furkuni. Baidyaram died leaving behind brother's son Raj Kanta. Thus, Raj Kanta acquired the entire property of the suit jote who died leaving behind mother Furkuni, wife Konok Prova and sister's son Suhal Chandra Sarker and Khagendra Nath Sarker. After the death of Raj Kanta, his wife Konok Prova embraced Islam and was married to a Muslim gentleman and lost her inheritance from Raj Kanta according to Hindu Law and as such, his mother Furkuni acquired all interest of Raj Kanta for her life time. Konok Prova sold schedule 'Ka' property by registered kabala dated 11.10.1946 to Subarna Lata Das and Sandhya Rani. But being aware of the legal status of Konok 'Prova, the purchasers again purchased the same property from Furkuni by registered kabala dated 14.12.1946. Both Konok Prova and Furkuni sold the suit property without any legal necessity and as such, those kabalas were not valid. Sandhya Rani and others settled the land to some of the defendants. Subsequently Furkuni died on 18.3.1973. Accordingly; after the death of Furkuni, the plaintiffs as the next reversioners inherited the entire property of Raj Kanta. Since both Konok Prova and Furkuni did not transfer the suit land for legal necessity, Subarna Lata and Sandhya Rani acquired no title and interest in the suit land. The plaintiffs demanded khas possession in the month of Chaitra, 1386 B.S. from the defendants, but they refused to do so. Hence, the plaintiffs instituted the suit for declaration of title and recovers of khas possession.
